# fivenines_wireguard_peers (Data Source)

The per-peer tunnel state behind the instance's VPN view -- which tunnel went quiet.

THE RAW PUBLIC KEY IS NEVER PUBLISHED. Identity is served two other ways: `key_digest` (16 hex chars of SHA-256 -- opaque, stable, survives a rename) and `display_name` (the wg-quick alias if the agent found one, else a short fingerprint). Key your own records on `key_digest`; `display_name` is operator-editable and is a label, not an identifier.

HANDSHAKE AGE ONLY MEANS SOMETHING NEXT TO `keepalive`. WireGuard is silent by design, so an idle peer with NO persistent keepalive can have an arbitrarily old handshake and be perfectly healthy -- alerting on age alone will page for healthy peers.

NULL IS "NO VERDICT", NEVER "0 SECONDS AGO". `handshake_age_seconds` falls back to `first_seen_at` when there has never been a handshake, so a freshly-added peer reads a small age WITHOUT being active -- read `handshake_active` for "is this tunnel carrying traffic".

This collector is config-driven with no version floor, so `collector.supported` here means "the agent has not said it cannot".

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_wireguard_peers" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.vpn.id
}

# Key your own records on key_digest. The raw public key is never published,
# and display_name is operator-editable -- a label, not an identifier.
output "peer_names" {
  value = {
    for p in data.fivenines_wireguard_peers.all.wireguard_peers :
    p.key_digest => p.display_name
  }
}

# Handshake age only means something next to keepalive: WireGuard is silent by
# design, so an idle peer without a persistent keepalive can have an
# arbitrarily old handshake and be perfectly healthy.
output "quiet_keepalive_peers" {
  value = [
    for p in data.fivenines_wireguard_peers.all.wireguard_peers :
    p.display_name if p.keepalive && !p.handshake_active
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `interface` (String) Return only the peers on this WireGuard interface.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the display name, endpoint or allowed IPs -- deliberately never the public key.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over the collector's 10-minute sync window. `false` returns only rows the agent refreshed inside it -- the set you may read as CURRENT state; `true` returns the rest. The two values partition the collection (a row that never synced counts as stale). Omit for both.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `wireguard_peers` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--wireguard_peers))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--wireguard_peers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `wireguard_peers`

Read-Only:

- `allowed_ips` (String) The peer's routed subnets.
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `display_name` (String) The wg-quick `# Name =` alias when the agent found one, else a short key fingerprint. Operator-editable, so a label rather than an identifier.
- `endpoint` (String) The peer's real public IP:port as the kernel last saw it. Null before the first handshake, and it moves for a roaming peer.
- `fingerprint` (String) 8 leading base64 characters of the key plus an ellipsis -- the same short form the dashboard renders, so an operator reading a log line and an operator reading the UI are looking at the same peer. It is DERIVED FROM the public key, not opaque: 48 of its 256 bits. That is enough to identify a peer within one interface and not enough to be the key, but treat it as key-derived rather than as a random handle. `id` is the stable opaque identifier; correlate on that.
- `first_seen_at` (String) When this peer first appeared. The fallback liveness anchor for a peer that has never handshaked.
- `handshake_active` (Boolean) A REAL handshake inside a fixed 3-minute window. Requires an actual handshake, so a never-connected peer is never active. This is the "is the tunnel carrying traffic" field.
- `handshake_age_seconds` (Number) Seconds since the last handshake, or since the peer first appeared when it has never handshaked -- so a freshly-added peer reads a small age without being active. Null only when neither anchor exists.
- `handshaked` (Boolean) Whether a real handshake has ever been recorded.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `interface` (String) The WireGuard interface the peer is configured on.
- `keepalive` (Boolean) LOAD-BEARING for reading the handshake fields. WireGuard is silent by design, so an idle peer WITHOUT keepalive can have an arbitrarily old handshake and be perfectly healthy -- alerting on age alone will page for healthy peers.
- `key_digest` (String) 16 hex chars of SHA-256 over the public key: opaque, stable, and the same correlation id the workflow triggers use. Key your records on THIS -- it survives a wg-quick rename. The raw public key is deliberately absent from this payload.
- `last_handshake_at` (String) Null = never handshaked since we started watching. Also reset by the kernel when an interface is recreated, which the ingester treats as forward-only so a wg-quick restart does not read as every peer going dark.
- `last_synced_at` (String) When the agent last refreshed this row.
- `persistent_keepalive` (Number) The configured keepalive interval in seconds, when set.
- `qualified_name` (String) interface/display_name -- a peer name is unique only within an interface.
- `rx_bytes` (Number) Cumulative bytes received from this peer.
- `stale` (Boolean) True when the agent stopped refreshing this row (outside the 10-minute sync window, or never synced). These tables are only updated while an agent keeps reporting, so a problem row on a dead agent reads as a problem forever -- check this before acting on the state above.
- `tx_bytes` (Number) Cumulative bytes sent to this peer.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
